title: Metering semantics for system messages, structured function-calls, and streaming fragments
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: We currently bill tokens by running a tokenizer pass at multiple places in the pipeline (API gateway, runtime ingress, and final reconciler) and then aggregating. This creates several incorrect and customer-visible edge cases: 1) system/admin messages that are present in request envelopes but are not intended to be billable are sometimes charged; 2) function-calling structured outputs (arguments / tool responses) may be double-counted when streamed in fragments or reassembled; 3) streaming fragments that are retransmitted during reconnect/resume create duplicate token tallies; 4) metadata fields (non-user visible trace headers or base64 blobs attached for routing/telemetry) are tokenized and incorrectly attributed.

Goal: Define deterministic, auditable metering semantics for all token sources in a request envelope and implement a minimal-change pipeline to enforce them with near-zero customer impact. We should preserve backward-compatibility for current billing reports while enabling more accurate attribution for Private/Dedicated customers who require exactness.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical token-attribution spec is written and approved by Billing and Runtime teams
API layer emits a single canonical tokenization event per logical request with token-tags (user|system|assistant|tool|meta)
Streaming fragments carry an idempotency sequence and are deduplicated before final crediting
Function-call arguments and tool outputs are attributed to the assistant role only when they are part of the final assistant response, otherwise tagged as tool and billed per tool rules
Billing reports show no statistically significant change for existing customers after canary, and edge-case spikes are resolved
Automated tests cover multipart streaming, reconnects, mid-stream model switches, and function-call chunking
notes: Design decisions: prefer single tokenizer source of truth at API ingress to avoid divergent tokenizers across languages; keep a lightweight token-tag ledger instead of passing raw text through billing path
We will not attempt to de-tokenize or re-parse semantics downstream; instead tags flow with tokenledgers and are consumed by reconciler
For Private installs where customers run their own tokenizer, provide an opt-in mode to accept pre-tagged ledgers from the runtime

Edge-case for prefix cache: cached prefixes that are replayed should carry a 'cached' flag and not be re-billed when used as part of a cached hit; when a cached prefix is modified by system augmentation it must be re-tokenized and billed appropriately
implementation_plan: Spec: draft canonical token-tag format and in-band sequence markers (Maya + Alex) - 2d
API: Emit canonical tokenization event at ingress, store ledger id in request context (Alex) - 3d
Runtime: honor ledger id, attach stream fragment sequence numbers to fragment events and dedupe on reconciler (SRE + Runtime) - 5d
Reconciler: single writer that consumes ledgers and performs final attribution with tags and idempotency checks (Billing team) - 4d
Tests: unit and e2e test harness for streaming reconnects, function-call chunking, cache hits - 3d
Canary: feature-flagged rollout to 5% of traffic with real-time billing sanity dashboard (Ops) - 2w
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Tokenizer mismatch between API and runtime causing small delta in token counts; Mitigation: run shadow tokenizer in runtime and log diffs for 1w; if diff >0.5% hold rollout
Risk: Increased latency at API ingress due to tokenization; Mitigation: async tokenization for low-priority routes and batching for bursty clients
Risk: Legacy billing consumers expecting previous attribution fields; Mitigation: provide a migration adapter and keep old aggregated counts for 90 days under 'legacy_total' column in billing exports
tests: Unit: tokenizer tagging logic with synthetic inputs covering unicode, emojis, long prompts
Integration: simulated streaming client that sends function-call args in fragmented frames, then reconnects and resumes; assert single final charge
E2E: Canary traffic run with synthetic load matching customer patterns and verify billing export matches expected ledger within tolerance
Regression: run existing billing reconciliation jobs and validate no unexplained deltas (>0.2%) across top 50 customers
